To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CAS probe and FSSP were able to measure the same cloud droplet size distribution and sizing parameters (effective and median volume diameters) in a good agreement.

the FSSP and CAS probes have good agreement in deriving size distribution and sizing parameters, however CAS probe loses significant amount of cloud water in sub-Arctica when the wind direction is out of wind iso-axial conditions.

CAS and FSPS-100 are suitable instruments for measuring cloud properties in sub-Arctis conditions, but the CAS probe is not suitable to measure cloud droplets smaller than 5 µm in diameter and the CDP is not suitable in sub-Arctica conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the CAS and FSSPs in sub-Arctica conditions.
the performance of three different cloud probes under sub-zero conditions.
the evaluation of ground based cloud spectrometers and the results can be applied in future campaigns where focus is set on investigating the effect of aerosol-cloud interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAS probe is not suitable for cloud measurements in sub-Aractic region in sub-zero temperatures due to its sensitivity to wind direction.

the FSSP and CDP were more suitable for cloud droplet size distribution measurements in the sub-zero temperatures and the CAS probe was more suitable for cloud size distribution measurements in sub-zero temperatures when the wind direction is within the wind iso axial conditions.
the CAS probe is a good instrument for cloud measurements in sub-Arctics, but it is sensitive to wind direction and temperature conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CAS probe can be used in campaigns where the main focus is on aerosol cloud interactions but the FSSP probe would be the best instrument for deriving the liquid water content in the sub-Arctic regions.
the CAS probe is a reliable instrument in measuring cloud droplet size distribution and sizing parameters in the size range of 5 to 50 µm.
the CAS probe was not suitable for measurements in sub-zero conditions and the FSSPP-100 and the CAS probe had good agreement in sizing parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAS probe should be placed on a rotating table to ensure that it is sampling cloud droplets in the same way as the FSSP and the CDP probes.
the CDP probe should be operated only in sub-zero conditions with a wind shield.
the FSSP is more sensitive to the wind direction in comparison to CAS.
